meetings.title: Durham Joint City-County Planning Committee - June 1, 2022
meetings.executive_summary: The June 1, 2022 Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) meeting marked the committee's return to in-person sessions at 9:30 AM, opened with Pride Month remarks and a roll-call vote approving the April 6, 2022 meeting minutes. Planning Director Sara Young introduced Item 7, a privately initiated Unified Development Ordinance text amendment led by developer Jim Anthony, Aaron Lubeck, and Dave Albertson aimed at simplifying standards and adding flexibility for small-scale infill development, noting applicants and staff were already iterating on revisions. Following a middle section truncated in the digest, committee members and staff reviewed draft Comprehensive Plan policies addressing state statutory boundaries, Durham Housing Authority resident relocation during redevelopment, evaluating public land for housing and public goods, and income-tier housing goals. Council Member Javiera Caballero commended staff for an open process extending beyond traditional land-use policy before the committee adjourned at 11:19 AM.

agenda_items.title: Return to In-Person Session, Pride Month Remarks, and Approval of April 6, 2022 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Chair convened the Joint City-County Planning Committee's first in-person meeting back in chambers at 9:30 AM, recognized staff for coordinating the return, and extended Pride Month greetings on behalf of the Mayor and administration. A motion from Commissioner Burns, seconded by Chairman Dola (ASR), to approve the April 6, 2022 minutes proceeded to a clerk roll-call vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Roll Call; tally omitted in digest)

agenda_items.title: Privately Initiated Text Amendment for Small-Scale Infill Development
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Sara Young introduced a privately initiated UDO text amendment intended to simplify development regulations and add flexibility for organic, small-scale infill, noting the applicants were already revising the proposal to address staff memo concerns. Jim Anthony—accompanied by Aaron Lubeck and Dave Albertson—outlined the coalition's 25-year context in Durham real estate and plans for broad public dialogue before opening for committee questions prior to the middle truncation.

agenda_items.title: Draft Comprehensive Plan Policy Review (Relocation, Public Land, and Housing Tiers)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed draft Comprehensive Plan vision statements and action items covering state statutory limits on local rules, Durham Housing Authority resident relocation protections during redevelopment, assessing public land uses for housing and public goods, accessible linear public spaces, and addressing different housing income tiers without over-restricting the plan. Staff outlined plans to revise policies over the summer based on community feedback, Javiera Caballero praised the broad, dynamic process, and the Chair adjourned the meeting at 11:19 AM.

votes.item_title: Approve Minutes from the April 6, 2022 Joint City-County Planning Committee Meeting
votes.notes: Joint City-County Planning Committee meeting (includes City Council and County/Planning representatives); mover/seconder were non-City-Council committee members ('commissioner burns', 'chairman dola' per ASR) and individual roll-call responses were masked by music/omitted in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: With no amendments or corrections offered to the April 6, 2022 Joint City-County Planning Committee minutes, the Chair received a motion from Commissioner Burns and a second from Chairman Dola (ASR) and directed the clerk to call the roll.

meetings.title: Joint City County Planning Committee - April 6, 2022
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton, the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) met with City Council Member DeDreana Freeman, alternate Leonardo Williams (who joined later in the session), and Durham County and Planning Commission counterparts, while granting Council Member Javiera Caballero an excused absence 5-0. The Committee unanimously recommended approval 7-0 of the FY 2023 Planning Department Work Program emphasizing Comprehensive Plan implementation, a new Racial Equity and Inclusion Action Plan, and affordable housing coordination. Staff also briefed the Committee on withdrawing Natural Heritage Area UDO regulatory language due to state Nature Preserves Act restrictions, presented Comprehensive Plan Place Type and Urban Growth Boundary revisions removing roughly 13 square miles due to water/sewer extension limits, and gathered early feedback on streamlining UDO development plan rules and Expanding Housing Choices (EHC) permitting metrics.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence for Javiera Caballero, and Approval of February 2, 2022 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Mark-Anthony Middleton convened the virtual JCCPC session with Council Member DeDreana Freeman, Durham County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Brenda Howerton, and Planning Commissioner Austin Amendola present (with County Commissioner Nida Allam/Burns and alternate Council Member Leonardo Williams joining later). The Committee voted 5-0 to grant Javiera Caballero an excused absence and 5-0 to approve the February 2, 2022 minutes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-0 (2 votes: excused absence and minutes)

agenda_items.title: Natural Heritage Areas UDO Text Amendment Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning supervisor Michael Stock and NC Natural Heritage Program Director Misty Buchanan explained that North Carolina's Nature Preserves Act prohibits local governments from using state Natural Heritage Inventory data for mandatory land-use regulation, limiting participation to voluntary landowner conservation agreements. Planning Director Sara Young confirmed staff pulled the regulatory UDO text amendment and would instead pursue updated city/county open space master plans, while County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs urged funding an independent local inventory and Council Member DeDreana Freeman asked about Heron Rookery protections and the requested DOST open space implementer position.

agenda_items.title: FY 2023 Planning Department Work Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Sara Young and Grace Smith presented the FY 2023 Work Program transitioning from drafting the Comprehensive Plan toward UDO overhaul implementation and a departmental Racial Equity and Inclusion Action Plan. Members discussed coordinating an open space/real estate implementer position and expediting affordable housing reviews before recommending approval of the work program.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Update: Draft Policies, Place Type Map, and Urban Growth Boundary
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planners Carl Kolosna, Lisa Miller, and Scott Whiteman reviewed fall-winter Place Type Map engagement, technical corrections converting protected easements to Recreation and Open Space, and 228 draft policies scheduled for spring public engagement. Staff proposed shrinking the Urban Growth Boundary by roughly 13 square miles across areas such as Arrowhead, Umstead Road, Snow Hill Road, far East Durham, and Southwest Durham where water and sewer extension is cost-prohibitive, receiving informal committee consensus to proceed.

agenda_items.title: Development Plan Revisions UDO Text Amendment Concept
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined early concept ideas to shorten and simplify zoning map change procedures, including making pre-submittal meetings optional, expanding text-only development plans to avoid up to $50,000 in site engineering fees on graphic plans, removing low-value proffers, and letting the Planning Director require extra neighborhood meetings. Committee members discussed tying streamlined review thresholds to meaningful affordable housing commitments.

agenda_items.title: Expanding Housing Choices (EHC) Implementation Metrics
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planners Scott Whiteman and Sara Young reported 237 EHC permits issued through Q4 2021—including 49 ADUs, 45 small-lot houses, and 93 lot splits—and 99 residential demolitions in 2021, only 11 of which were EHC-related. Alternate Council Member Leonardo Williams, Commissioner Jacobs, and Planning Commissioner Amendola discussed ADU pattern books and triplex/fourplex barriers, with Williams arguing piecemeal rules have not yet met Durham's housing affordability crisis and requesting a deeper follow-up review.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Council Member Javiera Caballero (JCCPC)
votes.notes: Tally 5-0 reflects seated City Council JCCPC members Middleton and Freeman plus Durham County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Brenda Howerton and Planning Commissioner Austin Amendola. Leonardo Williams attended later as alternate.
votes.discussion_detail: Joint City-County Planning Committee roll call excusing Caballero due to illness.

votes.notes: Tally 5-0 includes Middleton and Freeman alongside non-City JCCPC members Jacobs, Howerton, and Amendola.

votes.item_title: Recommend Approval of Proposed FY 2023 Planning Department Work Program
votes.notes: JCCPC tally 7-0 includes City Council JCCPC members Middleton and Freeman alongside participating Durham County Commissioners (including Burns/Allam who joined at 00:35:56) and Planning Commission members.
votes.discussion_detail: Recommends the FY 2023 City-County Planning Department Work Program advancing Comprehensive Plan implementation and racial equity initiatives.

meetings.title: Joint City County Planning Committee Feb. 2, 2022
meetings.executive_summary: The Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) met with Immediate Past Chair Wendy Jacobs opening the session before rotating the annual chairmanship to City Council Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton (6-0) and electing Durham County Commissioner Nimasheena Burns as Vice Chair (6-0). Committee members excused Commissioner Brenda Howerton's absence (6-0), approved December 1, 2021 minutes (6-0), and deferred Item 14 (Natural Heritage Areas UDO text amendment) to April. JCCPC received five 2021 annual board reports (Appearance Commission, Board of Adjustment, Planning Commission, DOST, and Historic Preservation Commission) alongside four major planning briefings: Comprehensive Plan engagement (~1,300 unique visitors and 341 surveys on the draft Place Type Map) and Braggtown coordination, a connectivity/block-length UDO scoping update, unified hybrid/in-person Neighborhood Meeting Guidelines requiring 600-foot mailed notices and recordings, and mandatory removal of criminal penalties from land-use ordinances under NC Session Law 2021-138.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absence, Minutes & Officer Elections (Items 1-7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Immediate Past Chair Commissioner Wendy Jacobs confirmed quorum with City members Mark-Anthony Middleton, DeDreana Freeman, and Javiera Caballero (with Leonardo Williams designated alternate), County Commissioner Nimasheena Burns, and Planning Commission Chair Austin Amandolia. The committee excused Commissioner Brenda Howerton's absence (6-0), deferred Item 14 to April, approved December 1, 2021 minutes (6-0), and elected Mark-Anthony Middleton Chair (6-0) and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns Vice Chair (6-0).

agenda_items.title: 2021 Annual Reports: Appearance Commission, Board of Adjustment & Planning Commission (Items 8-10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planners Kayla Seibel, Jessica Dockery, and Michael Stock joined commission chairs Brant Smith and Austin Amandolia to present 2021 annual reports: Appearance Commission's Golden Leaf revival and virtual meetings; Board of Adjustment's review of variance/special-use caseloads; and Planning Commission's 47-51 zoning/text amendment cases across 13 virtual meetings alongside recommendations on missing-middle housing and equitable transit corridors.

agenda_items.title: 2021 Annual Reports: DOST & Historic Preservation Commission (Items 11-12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff Carl Kolosna and DOST Chair Laura Stroud reviewed open-space preservation, trails staffing priorities, and equity alignment, followed by Carla Rosenberg and Historic Preservation Commission Chair Matt Bouchard reporting on Certificates of Appropriateness, historic district updates (Golden Belt, East Durham, College View), and outreach.

agenda_items.title: Item 13: Comprehensive Plan Place Type Map Engagement & Policy Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Kayla Seibel and Planning Manager Scott Whiteman reported 4,300+ site visits (~1,300 unique visitors) and 341 surveys on the draft Place Type Map (extended through March 1 with Ambassador Idea Ortiz), six active policy working groups, and Braggtown Community Association outreach. Committee members debated place-type granularity, shrinking peripheral Urban Growth Boundary future-growth areas to prevent sprawl vs enabling infill height/missing-middle housing, and preserving affordable housing tools like density bonuses.

agenda_items.title: Item 15: Block Length and Connectivity UDO Text Amendment Scoping
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planners Brooke Roper and Michael Stock presented scoping analysis on updating Durham's street link-node ratio, pedestrian connectivity, and block-length standards following Planning Commission's resolution. Members cautioned against one-size-fits-all acreage mandates in rural unincorporated tracts and urged assessing construction cost impacts on housing affordability.

agenda_items.title: Items 16 & 17: Neighborhood Meeting Guidelines & Session Law 2021-138 Compliance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Grace Smith presented consolidated Neighborhood Meeting Guidelines offering full-virtual or hybrid formats, correcting an erroneous pre-application citation, and newly requiring recordings plus first-class mailed notices within 600 feet directing residents to Social Pinpoint. Michael Stock previewed omnibus UDO amendments required by NC Session Law 2021-138 to remove criminal penalties (retaining civil fines) for land-use ordinance violations.
